text: Dean Withers was accused of R.A.P.E. So what were the political reactions on the left and on the right? Let's start with the right. Some people seem to genuinely believe Dean is guilty. And few are actually defending him. But one of the most visible reactions are something like, now you know how it feels. Taste of your own medicine. Believe women. Or believe victims. And that's an important distinction. A lot of these people aren't necessarily saying Dean is guilty. They are saying, you helped promote a culture where accusations could destroy somebody. And now those same rules are being applied to you. But is that actually fair? I did some checking. Despite people constantly throwing believe all women and believe victims at Dean, I couldn't actually find Dean himself saying every accusation should automatically be believed. Maybe somebody can find me a clip that I missed, but based on what I could find, I don't think it's fair to simply put that position in his mouth. People also point out that Dean repeatedly called Donald Trump an R.A.P.E.ist. And yes, he has. But I don't think that's a very good example of hypocrisy. A civil jury did find Trump liable for sexually abusing Agent Carroll. And while the jury did not find R.A.P.E. under the narrow New York legal definition used at the time, the judge later said, the conduct the jury found amounted to R.A.P.E. under the ordinary meaning of the word and that Carroll's statements were substantially true. So Dean wasn't simply taking an anonymous accusation and declaring Trump guilty. However, there is a stronger example. Dean has also called Trump a pedophile. And unlike the Carroll case, I haven't found evidence establishing that Trump abused a child. There are allegations involving minors and the Epstein connection, but that isn't the same thing as proving somebody is a pedophile. So if Dean's position now is, don't put an absolutely horrific label on me when the evidence doesn't establish it, I agree. But that standard has to work both ways. And Dean may be doing something similar right now. He said, a Trump supporter stole the identity of an innocent 13-year-old girl to falsely accuse me. But do we actually know that? We know MAGA and Groyper accounts massively amplified the accusations. But as far as I can tell, we still don't know who created the original Emily account. Maybe Dean has information that isn't public. But saying a Trump supporter created it goes beyond the public evidence. And that's pretty ironic. People take Dean was accused and jump to Dean did it. Dean takes MAGA amplified it and jumps to MAGA did it. Obviously, those accusations aren't equally serious, but the reasoning problem is similar, adding an unproven step and stating it as a fact. Now, what about the left? A lot of people on the left are defending Dean by saying the evidence looks fake or unverified and that you shouldn't destroy someone's reputation over an accusation. And they're right. But there is hypocrisy here too. Believe women and believe survivors were major slogans in progressive politics during Me Too, especially around the Kavanaugh allegations. There were nationwide believe survivors protests. Activists and prominent Democrats publicly declared that they believed his accusers before those allegations had actually been established. So if your standard then was basically, I believe her, but now that Dean is accused, your response is, where is the evidence? Then you've changed the standard depending on who is being accused. And the same applies to the right. If you spend years saying unproven accusations can destroy men's lives, but now you're spreading this one because you hate Dean, you are doing exactly what you criticized. And that's really my takeaway. SA and RAP allegations should be taken seriously, but taking them seriously is not the same as automatically believing them. Right now, I don't see credible evidence establishing that Dean committed what he's being accused of. If credible new evidence comes out, then we should update our conclusion. Innocent until proven guilty may be a legal principle, but it's also a pretty good rule before publicly calling someone an RAPist. Whether you like the person or not, look at the evidence.
